expectations.text: Activity: escalation has its own timeline — portents advance whether the party is present or not
expectations.evidence: Line 63: 'The freeze: Umberlee's escalation waits indefinitely.' Portents are party-triggered (port arrival), not time-driven. The quest explicitly implements the frozen-island pattern.

expectations.text: Early arrival produces different situation than mid or late arrival
expectations.evidence: The quest is identical regardless of when the party arrives. Line 63: 'Whether the party arrives at Kalowe tomorrow or six months later, the Dead Lady emerges the night after port arrival.'

expectations.text: Tide driven by Umberlee's established want and constraints, not by party arrival
expectations.evidence: Umberlee's want is established (Pearl retrieval) but the escalation mechanism is explicitly tied to party movement: 'manifests each night the party spends in port.' The tide mechanism is party-coupled.

expectations.text: Causality: each portent follows from the prior through Umberlee's methods (weather, Dead Lady, Waveservants)
expectations.evidence: Portents progress from taken-whole rumors → Delmar recognizes fog → Waveservants take notice → faces on the Dead Lady. Each uses Umberlee's established methods.

expectations.text: Quest frame names incompatible wants, live pressure, and uninterrupted consequence
expectations.evidence: Frame names Delmar's defiance vs Umberlee's demand, Dead Lady as pressure, and escalating consequences if unresolved.

expectations.text: Does not make the Dead Lady appear only upon party arrival at a port
expectations.evidence: Lines 62-63: 'The Dead Lady appears each night the party spends in port, manifesting in supernatural fog.' This is exactly the frozen-island pattern — the threat activates only on party action.
